audit.why: Emerald+ 50.55% over 821 games — an even lane that decays late, exactly what the text says.

Rumble owns levels 2-3, it evens out mid-lane, and Ryze takes over at two items. Ryze has no dash and no escape, so side lane and skirmishes stay Rumble's while he holds an item lead; teamfights are Equalizer-decided.

Level 2-3 pattern, level 6 Realm Warp, Liandry's first item, two-item Ryze takeover — all four spikes are real and correctly ordered. Realm Warp is 180/160/140s, which supports the 'track where he ports' framing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup calls Rune Prison a 'point-blank root' and treats it as an unconditional root. Both halves are wrong: it is 615 range, and it only roots when the target already has Flux on them — otherwise it is a slow.
audit.why: Riot's Rune Prison description: 'Ryze traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' Flux comes from Spell Flux (E), a 615-range orb on a 3.5s cooldown. That makes Spell Flux, not Rune Prison, the ability Rumble actually has to dodge — dodge the orb and the follow-up W is only a slow he can walk out of. Calling it point-blank is also actively harmful, because 615 range is longer than Flamespitter's 600 cone: Ryze can cast it from outside Rumble's damage.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[0], whys[2], wants.foe[1], spikes[3], dosFull[0].d, the Key Ability Interactions report line, and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere. 'Bait Rune Prison' with no duration attached is unactionable.
audit.why: Rune Prison is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s — a short window, so the advice has to be 'step in immediately', not 'wait'. Spell Flux is 3.5s and is effectively always up, which is why dodging the orb matters more than tracking the W.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with Rune Prison 11s, Spell Flux 3.5s and Realm Warp 180s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ryze having no dash was mentioned once in passing but never connected to The Equalizer.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this from Ryze's side: Rumble can cut his retreat and he has no dash to leave the wall. Placing the 1750-range Equalizer behind Ryze rather than on him is the concrete version of that.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now says to wall his retreat, not his face.

edits.after: 615 range, and it only roots if Spell Flux hit you first. Dodge the orb, then step in.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison: matchup-defining — His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rune Prison: 615 range, 11s at rank 1 — it roots only if Spell Flux is on you first, otherwise it is just a slow. - Spell Flux: 3.5s, the real tell. - Realm Warp: 180s. - The Equalizer: kill windows only.

notes: Rune Prison being conditional on Flux is the single fact this matchup was missing, and 'point-blank' was making players walk into a 615-range ability thinking they were safe at Flamespitter's 600 edge. The packet's suspectNames hit on "Rune Prison's" is a false positive — that is the correct name with a possessive. Standing note for Rumble: the kit file's knockup and terrain flags on Scrap Shield (W) are parsing misfires; Riot's description is a shield plus a speed burst only.
